independence_scope: intra-mesh Anthropic-family; agreement is corroboration, never cross-provider evidence

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived independently. sweep.py --web "Sabbath" returns exactly 1 verse book-wide (Ps.92.0), confirming the row's claim that this title is the book's only Sabbath-dedication superscription. psalm_device_inventory.json's genre_label_membership confirms Ps 92 sits in both the mizmor list (57 members) and the shir list (30 members, the post-erratum corrected count), matching the device_notes claim. The Hebrew title quote in the row collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.92.1. The span's closing boundary is sound: oshb:Ps.92.5 (web:Ps.92.4) opens with a causal particle plus a finite, suffixed verb ("you have made me glad") and direct address, a genuine register shift out of the infinitive-governed opening -- confirmed against both verse maps. However, the rationale's grammatical account of that infinitive-governed opening is wrong in its particulars (see challenge).

challenges.claim: The rationale's "three parallel infinitive clauses -- to give thanks, to proclaim loving kindness, and to play the instruments named at web:Ps.92.3" misidentifies the infinitives: it silently drops the second infinitive of oshb:Ps.92.2 and invents a nonexistent third infinitive for the verbless instrument list at oshb:Ps.92.4.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.92.2 = “ט֗וֹב לְהֹד֥וֹת לַיהוָ֑ה וּלְזַמֵּ֖ר לְשִׁמְךָ֣ עֶלְיֽוֹן” carries TWO infinitives (the "to give thanks" and "to sing praises" of WEB web:Ps.92.1, joined by "and"). oshb:Ps.92.3 = “לְהַגִּ֣יד בַּבֹּ֣קֶר חַסְֽדֶּ֑ךָ וֶ֝אֱמֽוּנָתְךָ֗ בַּלֵּילֽוֹת” carries ONE infinitive (WEB's "to proclaim" at web:Ps.92.2). oshb:Ps.92.4 = “עֲֽלֵי עָ֭שׂוֹר וַעֲלֵי נָ֑בֶל עֲלֵ֖י הִגָּי֣וֹן בְּכִנּֽוֹר”, rendered in WEB "with the ten-stringed lute, with the harp, and with the melody of the lyre" (web:Ps.92.3), is entirely verbless -- a bare prepositional list of instruments extending the earlier "to sing praises" clause, not a clause of its own. The count of three infinitives happens to be right, but "to sing praises" (WEB web:Ps.92.1's second clause) is never named, and "to play the instruments" is not a clause the Hebrew of web:Ps.92.3 contains. The span's actual boundary -- closing before the finite-verb, direct-address turn at web:Ps.92.4 -- is independently well-supported and is not in question.

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived. The causal particle opening oshb:Ps.92.5 (web:Ps.92.4) is byte-verified and correctly marks the pivot from the infinitive-governed opening into finite, addressed clauses. The rejected_alternative's claim that the fool's non-understanding (web:Ps.92.6) is completed by its object (web:Ps.92.7) checks out: oshb:Ps.92.7 ends with a forward-pointing demonstrative ("this") whose referent -- the wicked's flourishing followed by destruction -- is supplied only by the next verse; the two verses are one clause, not two independently standing ones. The closing boundary (web:Ps.92.8's adversative "but you" resuming direct address) is correctly identified and matches this row's own boundary_evidence_refs. All Hebrew quotes in the row collate at byte tier against their cited oshb refs. No defect found.

The address-frame argument for this span is sound: oshb:Ps.92.9 opens with an explicit independent second-person pronoun (byte-verified), distinct from the bound-suffix address used at oshb:Ps.92.5-6, and the span correctly closes where oshb:Ps.92.13's fronted, unaddressed subject ("the righteous") opens a class statement -- both quotes collate at byte tier, and Ps.92.13 is properly disclosed in boundary_evidence_refs since it is argued outside this row's own span. However, the rationale's content description for the span's interior is imprecise (see challenge).

challenges.claim: The rationale groups "the psalmist's own exaltation and anointing" under web:Ps.92.10-Ps.92.11, but only web:Ps.92.10 (oshb:Ps.92.11) carries exaltation/anointing content; web:Ps.92.11 (oshb:Ps.92.12) returns to the enemies theme, not exaltation.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.92.11 = “וַתָּ֣רֶם כִּרְאֵ֣ים קַרְנִ֑י בַּ֝לֹּתִ֗י בְּשֶׁ֣מֶן רַעֲנָֽן”, WEB "But you have exalted my horn like that of the wild ox. I am anointed with fresh oil." (web:Ps.92.10) -- the only verse in the span with exaltation/anointing vocabulary. oshb:Ps.92.12 = “וַתַּבֵּ֥ט עֵינִ֗י בְּשׁ֫וּרָ֥י בַּקָּמִ֖ים עָלַ֥י מְרֵעִ֗ים תִּשְׁמַ֥עְנָה אָזְנָֽי”, WEB "My eye has also seen my enemies. My ears have heard of the wicked enemies who rise up against me." (web:Ps.92.11) -- no exaltation or anointing term; a return to the enemies/foes theme paralleling web:Ps.92.9, not a continuation of the exaltation image. This does not affect the row's span boundaries, only its description of what web:Ps.92.11 contains.

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived. oshb:Ps.92.13's fronted subject ("the righteous... like the palm tree") opens a third-person gnomic image (byte-verified), correctly leaving behind the second-person address of the preceding span; the tree/temple-courts figure runs consistently through web:Ps.92.12-14 against the WEB text, and the psalm closes on the purpose clause at web:Ps.92.15. The device_notes' inclusio observation is explicitly hedged as thematic rather than verbatim repetition, which matches the actual wording -- there is no shared lexeme between web:Ps.92.1 and web:Ps.92.15's closing clauses. Tiling and boundary_evidence_refs are exact. No defect found.

The row's numerical claim is exceptionally well-supported: independently re-running the row's own skeleton sweep (its byte-verified opening phrase from oshb:Ps.93.1) returns exactly 6 verses book-wide (Ps.10.16, 29.10, 93.1, 96.10, 97.1, 99.1), and the pointed-verb-vs-noun distinction the row draws is confirmed exactly against the source bytes -- Ps.10.16 and Ps.29.10 carry the noun (segol-pattern) form, Ps.93.1/96.10/97.1/99.1 the verb (qamats-pattern) form -- so the narrowing from 6 to 4 and the "book's first of the 4" claim (93 precedes 96, 97, 99) both check out precisely. Ps 93 is confirmed an identity psalm with 5 WEB verses against web_mt_offset_map.json, so a whole_psalm row is policy-compliant regardless of the internal-cohesion argument below. However, the specific warrant offered for treating the psalm as internally undifferentiated is factually wrong (see challenge), and it is the row's stated basis for rejecting a split at web:Ps.93.2.

challenges.claim: observed_substrate_signals and rejected_alternative both assert "the psalm's five verses carry no second-person address" to argue the psalm has no internal seam, but oshb:Ps.93.2 and oshb:Ps.93.5 each carry direct second-person address to Yahweh.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.93.2 = “נָכ֣וֹן כִּסְאֲךָ֣ מֵאָ֑ז מֵֽעוֹלָ֣ם אָֽתָּה”, WEB "Your throne is established from long ago. You are from everlasting." (web:Ps.93.2) -- a bound second-person suffix on "throne" plus an independent second-person pronoun. oshb:Ps.93.5 = “עֵֽדֹתֶ֨יךָ נֶאֶמְנ֬וּ מְאֹ֗ד לְבֵיתְךָ֥ נַאֲוָה קֹ֑דֶשׁ יְ֝הוָ֗ה לְאֹ֣רֶךְ יָמִֽים”, WEB "Your statutes stand firm. Holiness adorns your house, Yahweh, forever more." (web:Ps.93.5) -- second-person suffixes on both "statutes" and "house." The claimed absence is false at two of the five verses. The correct pattern -- second-person address bracketing the third-person acclamation of web:Ps.93.1,3-4 -- would if anything argue FOR unity as an envelope structure rather than against a seam, but that is not the argument the row makes; as written, the warrant it gives for rejecting a split at web:Ps.93.2 does not hold.

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived. oshb:Ps.94.1's doubled-vocative claim is byte-verified -- the "God of vengeance" phrase occurs exactly twice in the verse, once addressed with the divine name and once resumed before the imperative "shine out," matching the row's claim of an intensified invocation. The span's internal move from direct address (web:Ps.94.1-3) to third-person description of the wicked's acts (web:Ps.94.5-6) to their quoted boast (web:Ps.94.7) is confirmed against the WEB text, and the closing boundary at the new imperative addressee (web:Ps.94.8, "Consider, you senseless...") is correctly identified. No defect found.

The span's opening and closing boundaries are sound: web:Ps.94.8's imperative addresses the senseless directly, distinct from the preceding complaint to Yahweh, and web:Ps.94.16's first-person opening reopens the psalm outside this span, correctly disclosed as the closing boundary. The macarism claim is verified: the "blessed" formula occurs exactly once within web:Ps.94.8-15 (at web:Ps.94.12), not repeated elsewhere in the span. However, the rejected_alternative's characterization of the whole span's addressee is overstated (see challenge).

challenges.claim: rejected_alternative describes web:Ps.94.8-Ps.94.15 as "addressed to a general audience rather than to Yahweh or in the first person," but web:Ps.94.12 embeds direct second-person address to Yah inside the beatitude's relative clause.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.94.12 = “אַשְׁרֵ֤י הַגֶּ֣בֶר אֲשֶׁר תְּיַסְּרֶ֣נּוּ יָּ֑הּ וּֽמִתּוֹרָתְךָ֥ תְלַמְּדֶֽנּוּ”, WEB "Blessed is the man whom you discipline, Yah, and teach out of your law," (web:Ps.94.12) -- two second-person verb forms and a second-person suffix on "your law" address Yah directly inside the third-person macarism. This is a brief embedded aside rather than a sustained address, so it does not by itself argue for splitting the span -- but the claim that the span holds no address to Yahweh is not accurate as stated.

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived. web:Ps.94.16's rhetorical "who" correctly marks the return to first-person testimony outside the preceding span. The row properly discloses (rather than conceals) the brief second-person aside at oshb:Ps.94.20 -- an interrogative-prefixed, second-person-suffixed verb form, byte-verified -- and treats it as texture rather than a boundary, a defensible call given it is a single rhetorical question bracketed by third-person material at web:Ps.94.21-22. The closing verse's repeated-verb claim is byte-verified: oshb:Ps.94.23's closing verb ("will cut them off") occurs twice in immediate succession, both instances preceding "Yahweh our God," exactly as the device_notes describe. The rejected_alternative's claim that web:Ps.94.16-19,22 share the same complaint against "the throne of wickedness" as web:Ps.94.20 is loosely put -- vv.17-19 are personal-testimony content without that specific image -- but this is a matter of degree in an already-hedged cohesion argument, not a false claim, and the span's boundaries and quotes are otherwise sound.
